newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists say EMU entry political, no dogma.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists say EMU entry political, no dogma.

text.p: French Socialist party economic policymaker Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Wednesday neither France nor Germany would meet all the criteria for a single European currency and the three percent deficit limit should not be treated as a dogma.

He also told Le Monde newspaper that France should rely on boosting purchasing power to stimulate the economy, since this could not be achieved through interest rates and it was hard to see how of raise growth through budgetary measures.
"Economic stimulation through monetary policy is barred, budgetary stimulation is hard to see, what's left is stimulation through a boost in purchasing power," he told Le Monde.
Strauss-Kahn, co-author of Socialist economic policy, spelled out his party's views as campaigning begins for a snap parliamentary election in two rounds on May 25 and June 1.
"We want the single (European) currency. What we want is an instrument that allows us counterbalance American domination and help growth and employment," he said.

"As far as the (monetary union) criteria are concerned, neither Germany nor France, to mention but two, will respect them all. A political decision will therefore apply, I hope. Even if it's clear public deficits cannot be allowed to slip, there is no point making an unjustified dogma out of the three percent (deficit limit) criterion," he said.
